True Statement: Endocrine glands lack ducts and are hence called ductless glands; their secretions are called hormones.
False 1: Exocrine glands lack ducts and are hence called ductless glands.

True Statement: Hormones are non-nutrient chemicals which act as intercellular messengers and are produced in trace amounts.
False 1: Hormones are nutrient chemicals which act as intercellular messengers and are produced in trace amounts.
False 2: Hormones are non-nutrient chemicals which act as intracellular messengers and are produced in trace amounts.

True Statement: Invertebrates possess very simple endocrine systems with few hormones, whereas a large number of chemicals act as hormones in vertebrates.
False 1: Vertebrates possess very simple endocrine systems with few hormones, whereas a large number of chemicals act as hormones in invertebrates.

True Statement: The hypothalamus is the basal part of diencephalon, forebrain, and it regulates a wide spectrum of body functions.
False 1: The hypothalamus is the basal part of telencephalon, forebrain.
False 2: The pituitary gland is the basal part of diencephalon, forebrain.

True Statement: The hypothalamus contains several groups of neurosecretory cells called nuclei which produce hormones that regulate the synthesis and secretion of pituitary hormones.
False 1: The pituitary gland contains several groups of neurosecretory cells called nuclei which produce hormones that regulate the synthesis and secretion of hypothalamic hormones.

True Statement: Hypothalamic hormones are of two types: releasing hormones (which stimulate secretion of pituitary hormones) and inhibiting hormones (which inhibit secretions of pituitary hormones).
False 1: Releasing hormones inhibit secretion of pituitary hormones, while inhibiting hormones stimulate secretion of pituitary hormones.
False 2: Hypothalamic hormones are of three types: releasing hormones, inhibiting hormones, and stimulating hormones.

True Statement: Gonadotrophin releasing hormone (GnRH) stimulates the pituitary synthesis and release of gonadotrophins.
False 1: Gonadotrophin releasing hormone (GnRH) inhibits the pituitary synthesis and release of gonadotrophins.
False 2: Somatostatin stimulates the pituitary synthesis and release of gonadotrophins.

True Statement: Somatostatin from the hypothalamus inhibits the release of growth hormone from the pituitary.
False 1: GnRH from the hypothalamus inhibits the release of growth hormone from the pituitary.
False 2: Somatostatin from the hypothalamus stimulates the release of growth hormone from the pituitary.

True Statement: Hypothalamic hormones reach the pituitary gland through a portal circulatory system and regulate the functions of the anterior pituitary.
False 1: Hypothalamic hormones reach the pituitary gland through a portal circulatory system and regulate the functions of the posterior pituitary.

True Statement: The posterior pituitary is under the direct neural regulation of the hypothalamus.
False 1: The anterior pituitary is under the direct neural regulation of the hypothalamus.

True Statement: The pituitary gland is located in a bony cavity called sella tursica and is attached to the hypothalamus by a stalk.
False 1: The pituitary gland is located in a bony cavity called the foramen magnum.
False 2: The pineal gland is located in a bony cavity called sella tursica and is attached to the hypothalamus by a stalk.

True Statement: The pituitary is divided into adenohypophysis and neurohypophysis; adenohypophysis consists of two portions, pars distalis and pars intermedia.
False 1: The pituitary is divided into adenohypophysis and neurohypophysis; neurohypophysis consists of two portions, pars distalis and pars intermedia.

True Statement: Pars distalis (anterior pituitary) produces GH, PRL, TSH, ACTH, LH and FSH.
False 1: Pars intermedia produces GH, PRL, TSH, ACTH, LH and FSH.
False 2: Neurohypophysis (posterior pituitary) produces GH, PRL, TSH, ACTH, LH and FSH.

True Statement: Pars intermedia secretes only one hormone called melanocyte stimulating hormone (MSH).
False 1: Pars distalis secretes only one hormone called melanocyte stimulating hormone (MSH).
False 2: Pars intermedia secretes only one hormone called growth hormone (GH).

True Statement: Neurohypophysis (posterior pituitary) stores and releases two hormones, oxytocin and vasopressin, which are actually synthesised by the hypothalamus and transported axonally.
False 1: Neurohypophysis stores and releases two hormones, oxytocin and vasopressin, which are actually synthesised by the anterior pituitary.
False 2: Neurohypophysis stores and releases two hormones, MSH and vasopressin, which are actually synthesised by the hypothalamus.

True Statement: Over-secretion of GH stimulates abnormal growth leading to gigantism; low secretion of GH results in stunted growth causing pituitary dwarfism.
False 1: Over-secretion of GH results in stunted growth (pituitary dwarfism); low secretion of GH causes gigantism.
False 2: Over-secretion of TSH stimulates abnormal growth leading to gigantism.

True Statement: Excess secretion of GH in adults (especially in middle age) causes severe disfigurement called Acromegaly.
False 1: Excess secretion of GH in children causes severe disfigurement called Acromegaly.
False 2: Excess secretion of ACTH in adults causes severe disfigurement called Acromegaly.

True Statement: Prolactin regulates the growth of the mammary glands and formation of milk in them.
False 1: Oxytocin regulates the growth of the mammary glands and formation of milk in them.
False 2: TSH regulates the growth of the mammary glands and formation of milk in them.

True Statement: TSH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of thyroid hormones from the thyroid gland.
False 1: ACTH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of thyroid hormones from the thyroid gland.
False 2: TSH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of glucocorticoids from the adrenal cortex.

True Statement: ACTH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of steroid hormones called glucocorticoids from the adrenal cortex.
False 1: TSH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of glucocorticoids from the adrenal cortex.
False 2: ACTH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of thyroid hormones from the thyroid gland.

True Statement: LH and FSH stimulate gonadal activity and hence are called gonadotrophins.
False 1: TSH and ACTH stimulate gonadal activity and hence are called gonadotrophins.

True Statement: In males, LH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of androgens from testis.
False 1: In males, FSH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of androgens from testis.
False 2: In females, LH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of androgens from testis.

True Statement: In males, FSH and androgens regulate spermatogenesis.
False 1: In males, LH and androgens regulate spermatogenesis.
False 2: In females, FSH and androgens regulate spermatogenesis.

True Statement: In females, LH induces ovulation of fully mature follicles (graafian follicles) and maintains the corpus luteum.
False 1: In females, FSH induces ovulation of fully mature follicles (graafian follicles) and maintains the corpus luteum.
False 2: In females, LH stimulates growth and development of the ovarian follicles.

True Statement: FSH stimulates growth and development of the ovarian follicles in females.
False 1: LH stimulates growth and development of the ovarian follicles in females.

True Statement: MSH acts on melanocytes (melanin containing cells) and regulates pigmentation of the skin.
False 1: TSH acts on melanocytes and regulates pigmentation of the skin.
False 2: MSH acts on melanocytes and regulates blood calcium levels.

True Statement: Oxytocin acts on smooth muscles and stimulates their contraction; in females it stimulates vigorous contraction of uterus at childbirth and milk ejection from the mammary gland.
False 1: Vasopressin acts on smooth muscles and stimulates their contraction; in females it stimulates vigorous contraction of uterus at childbirth and milk ejection.
False 2: Oxytocin acts on smooth muscles and stimulates their relaxation; in females it stimulates uterus contraction at childbirth.

True Statement: Vasopressin (ADH) acts mainly at the kidney and stimulates resorption of water and electrolytes by the distal tubules, thereby reducing loss of water through urine.
False 1: Oxytocin acts mainly at the kidney and stimulates resorption of water and electrolytes by the distal tubules.
False 2: Vasopressin (ADH) acts mainly at the kidney and stimulates excretion of water and electrolytes by the distal tubules, thereby increasing loss of water through urine.

True Statement: Impairment of ADH synthesis or release results in a diminished ability of the kidney to conserve water, causing water loss and dehydration – a condition called Diabetes Insipidus.
False 1: Impairment of ADH synthesis results in excessive water conservation by the kidney – a condition called Diabetes Insipidus.
False 2: Impairment of insulin synthesis or release results in a diminished ability of the kidney to conserve water – a condition called Diabetes Insipidus.

True Statement: The pineal gland is located on the dorsal side of the forebrain.
False 1: The pineal gland is located on the ventral side of the forebrain.
False 2: The pituitary gland is located on the dorsal side of the forebrain.

True Statement: Pineal secretes a hormone called melatonin.
False 1: Pineal secretes a hormone called serotonin.

True Statement: Melatonin plays a very important role in the regulation of the 24-hour (diurnal) rhythm of the body, including the sleep-wake cycle and body temperature.
False 1: Melatonin plays a very important role in the regulation of the monthly (menstrual) rhythm of the body.
False 2: TSH plays a very important role in the regulation of the 24-hour (diurnal) rhythm of the body.

True Statement: The thyroid gland is composed of two lobes located on either side of the trachea, interconnected with a thin flap of connective tissue called isthmus.
False 1: The thyroid gland is composed of two lobes located on either side of the trachea, interconnected with a thin flap of connective tissue called thymus.
False 2: The parathyroid gland is composed of two lobes located on either side of the trachea, interconnected by an isthmus.

True Statement: Each thyroid follicle is composed of follicular cells, enclosing a cavity; these follicular cells synthesise tetraiodothyronine (T₄) and triiodothyronine (T₃).
False 1: Each thyroid follicle synthesises tetraiodothyronine (T₄) and diiodothyronine (T₂).
False 2: Each parathyroid follicle is composed of follicular cells that synthesise T₄ and T₃.

True Statement: Iodine is essential for the normal rate of thyroid hormone synthesis; deficiency of iodine results in hypothyroidism and enlargement of the thyroid gland, commonly called goitre.
False 1: Calcium is essential for the normal rate of thyroid hormone synthesis; deficiency of calcium results in hypothyroidism and goitre.
False 2: Deficiency of iodine results in hyperthyroidism and enlargement of the thyroid gland, commonly called goitre.

True Statement: Hypothyroidism during pregnancy causes cretinism (stunted growth), mental retardation, low IQ, abnormal skin, and deaf-mutism.
False 1: Hyperthyroidism during pregnancy causes cretinism (stunted growth) and mental retardation.
False 2: Hypothyroidism during pregnancy causes gigantism, high IQ, and normal skin development in the growing baby.

True Statement: In adult women, hypothyroidism may cause the menstrual cycle to become irregular.
False 1: In adult women, hyperthyroidism may cause the menstrual cycle to become irregular.

True Statement: Exophthalmic goitre (Graves' disease) is a form of hyperthyroidism characterised by enlargement of the thyroid gland, protrusion of eyeballs, increased basal metabolic rate, and weight loss.
False 1: Graves' disease is a form of hypothyroidism characterised by enlargement of the thyroid gland and protrusion of eyeballs.
False 2: Exophthalmic goitre is a form of hyperthyroidism characterised by decreased basal metabolic rate and weight gain.

True Statement: Thyroid hormones play an important role in the regulation of the basal metabolic rate and support the process of red blood cell formation.
False 1: Parathyroid hormones play an important role in the regulation of the basal metabolic rate and support red blood cell formation.
False 2: Thyroid hormones play an important role in the regulation of blood calcium levels and support the process of red blood cell formation.

True Statement: Thyroid hormones control the metabolism of carbohydrates, proteins and fats, and also influence maintenance of water and electrolyte balance.
False 1: Parathyroid hormones control the metabolism of carbohydrates, proteins and fats, and also influence maintenance of water and electrolyte balance.

True Statement: The thyroid gland also secretes a protein hormone called thyrocalcitonin (TCT) which regulates blood calcium levels.
False 1: The parathyroid gland also secretes thyrocalcitonin (TCT) which regulates blood calcium levels.
False 2: The thyroid gland secretes thyrocalcitonin (TCT) which increases blood calcium levels.

True Statement: In humans, four parathyroid glands are present on the back side of the thyroid gland, one pair each in the two lobes of the thyroid gland.
False 1: In humans, two parathyroid glands are present on the back side of the thyroid gland.
False 2: In humans, four parathyroid glands are present on the front side of the thyroid gland.

True Statement: The parathyroid glands secrete a peptide hormone called parathyroid hormone (PTH), whose secretion is regulated by the circulating levels of calcium ions.
False 1: The parathyroid glands secrete a steroid hormone called parathyroid hormone (PTH).
False 2: The secretion of PTH is regulated by the circulating levels of sodium ions.

True Statement: PTH increases Ca²⁺ levels in the blood and acts on bones to stimulate the process of bone resorption (dissolution/demineralisation).
False 1: PTH decreases Ca²⁺ levels in the blood and acts on bones to inhibit the process of bone resorption.
False 2: TCT increases Ca²⁺ levels in the blood and acts on bones to stimulate bone resorption.

True Statement: PTH stimulates reabsorption of Ca²⁺ by the renal tubules and increases Ca²⁺ absorption from digested food; thus PTH is a hypercalcemic hormone.
False 1: PTH stimulates excretion of Ca²⁺ by the renal tubules and decreases Ca²⁺ absorption from digested food; thus PTH is a hypocalcemic hormone.
False 2: PTH stimulates reabsorption of Na⁺ by the renal tubules and increases Na⁺ absorption from digested food.

True Statement: The thymus gland is a lobular structure located between the lungs behind the sternum on the ventral side of the aorta.
False 1: The thymus gland is a lobular structure located between the lungs behind the sternum on the dorsal side of the aorta.
False 2: The pineal gland is a lobular structure located between the lungs behind the sternum on the ventral side of the aorta.

True Statement: The thymus secretes peptide hormones called thymosins which play a major role in the differentiation of T-lymphocytes, providing cell-mediated immunity.
False 1: The thymus secretes peptide hormones called thymosins which play a major role in the differentiation of B-lymphocytes.
False 2: The adrenal gland secretes peptide hormones called thymosins which play a major role in the differentiation of T-lymphocytes.

True Statement: Thymosins also promote production of antibodies to provide humoral immunity.
False 1: Thymosins inhibit the production of antibodies, suppressing humoral immunity.
False 2: Glucocorticoids promote production of antibodies to provide humoral immunity.

True Statement: Thymus degenerates in old individuals, resulting in decreased production of thymosins and weakened immune responses.
False 1: Thymus grows in old individuals, resulting in increased production of thymosins and strengthened immune responses.

True Statement: The body has one pair of adrenal glands, one above each kidney.
False 1: The body has one pair of adrenal glands, one below each kidney.

True Statement: The adrenal gland is composed of the centrally located adrenal medulla and the outer adrenal cortex.
False 1: The adrenal gland is composed of the centrally located adrenal cortex and the outer adrenal medulla.

True Statement: The adrenal medulla secretes adrenaline (epinephrine) and noradrenaline (norepinephrine), collectively called catecholamines.
False 1: The adrenal cortex secretes adrenaline (epinephrine) and noradrenaline (norepinephrine), collectively called catecholamines.
False 2: The adrenal medulla secretes cortisol and aldosterone, collectively called catecholamines.

True Statement: Adrenaline and noradrenaline are rapidly secreted in response to stress and emergency situations and are called emergency hormones or hormones of Fight or Flight.
False 1: Cortisol and aldosterone are rapidly secreted in response to stress and emergency situations and are called emergency hormones or hormones of Fight or Flight.

True Statement: Catecholamines increase alertness, pupilary dilation, piloerection, sweating, heart beat, strength of heart contraction and rate of respiration.
False 1: Thymosins increase alertness, pupilary dilation, piloerection, sweating, heart beat, strength of heart contraction and rate of respiration.
False 2: Catecholamines decrease alertness, cause pupilary constriction, and reduce heart beat and rate of respiration.

True Statement: Catecholamines stimulate the breakdown of glycogen resulting in an increased concentration of glucose in blood, and also stimulate breakdown of lipids and proteins.
False 1: Catecholamines stimulate the synthesis of glycogen resulting in a decreased concentration of glucose in blood.
False 2: Mineralocorticoids stimulate the breakdown of glycogen resulting in an increased concentration of glucose in blood.

True Statement: Underproduction of hormones by the adrenal cortex causes acute weakness and fatigue — a disease called Addison's disease.
False 1: Overproduction of hormones by the adrenal cortex causes acute weakness and fatigue — a disease called Addison's disease.
False 2: Underproduction of hormones by the adrenal medulla causes acute weakness and fatigue — a disease called Addison's disease.

True Statement: The adrenal cortex is divided into three layers: zona reticularis (inner), zona fasciculata (middle) and zona glomerulosa (outer).
False 1: The adrenal cortex is divided into three layers: zona glomerulosa (inner), zona fasciculata (middle) and zona reticularis (outer).
False 2: The adrenal medulla is divided into three layers: zona reticularis (inner), zona fasciculata (middle) and zona glomerulosa (outer).

True Statement: Glucocorticoids are corticoids involved in carbohydrate metabolism; cortisol is the main glucocorticoid.
False 1: Mineralocorticoids are corticoids involved in carbohydrate metabolism; cortisol is the main mineralocorticoid.
False 2: Glucocorticoids are corticoids involved in carbohydrate metabolism; aldosterone is the main glucocorticoid.

True Statement: Mineralocorticoids regulate the balance of water and electrolytes in the body; aldosterone is the main mineralocorticoid.
False 1: Glucocorticoids regulate the balance of water and electrolytes in the body; aldosterone is the main glucocorticoid.
False 2: Mineralocorticoids regulate the balance of water and electrolytes in the body; cortisol is the main mineralocorticoid.

True Statement: Glucocorticoids stimulate gluconeogenesis, lipolysis and proteolysis, and inhibit cellular uptake and utilisation of amino acids.
False 1: Mineralocorticoids stimulate gluconeogenesis, lipolysis and proteolysis, and inhibit cellular uptake and utilisation of amino acids.
False 2: Glucocorticoids stimulate gluconeogenesis, lipolysis and proteolysis, and enhance cellular uptake and utilisation of amino acids.

True Statement: Glucocorticoids (particularly cortisol) produce anti-inflammatory reactions and suppress the immune response; cortisol also stimulates RBC production.
False 1: Glucocorticoids produce pro-inflammatory reactions and enhance the immune response.
False 2: Thymosins produce anti-inflammatory reactions and suppress the immune response.

True Statement: Aldosterone acts mainly at the renal tubules and stimulates reabsorption of Na⁺ and water, and excretion of K⁺ and phosphate ions.
False 1: Cortisol acts mainly at the renal tubules and stimulates reabsorption of Na⁺ and water, and excretion of K⁺ and phosphate ions.
False 2: Aldosterone acts mainly at the renal tubules and stimulates excretion of Na⁺ and water, and reabsorption of K⁺ and phosphate ions.

True Statement: Small amounts of androgenic steroids secreted by the adrenal cortex play a role in growth of axial hair, pubic hair and facial hair during puberty.
False 1: Small amounts of androgenic steroids secreted by the adrenal medulla play a role in growth of axial hair, pubic hair and facial hair during puberty.

True Statement: Pancreas is a composite gland which acts as both exocrine and endocrine gland.
False 1: Thyroid is a composite gland which acts as both exocrine and endocrine gland.

True Statement: The endocrine pancreas consists of 'Islets of Langerhans'; there are about 1-2 million islets in a normal human pancreas, representing 1-2 per cent of the pancreatic tissue.
False 1: The endocrine pancreas consists of 'Islets of Langerhans', representing 10-20 per cent of the pancreatic tissue.
False 2: The endocrine pancreas consists of about 10-20 million Islets of Langerhans in a normal human pancreas.

True Statement: The α-cells of the Islet of Langerhans secrete glucagon, while the β-cells secrete insulin.
False 1: The α-cells secrete insulin, while the β-cells secrete glucagon.
False 2: The α-cells secrete glucagon, while the β-cells secrete thyroxine.

True Statement: Glucagon acts mainly on liver cells (hepatocytes) and stimulates glycogenolysis, resulting in increased blood sugar (hyperglycemia); it also stimulates gluconeogenesis.
False 1: Insulin acts mainly on liver cells and stimulates glycogenolysis, resulting in increased blood sugar (hyperglycemia).
False 2: Glucagon acts mainly on liver cells and stimulates glycogenesis, resulting in decreased blood sugar (hypoglycemia).

True Statement: Glucagon reduces cellular glucose uptake and utilisation; thus glucagon is a hyperglycemic hormone.
False 1: Glucagon enhances cellular glucose uptake and utilisation; thus glucagon is a hypoglycemic hormone.
False 2: Insulin reduces cellular glucose uptake and utilisation; thus insulin is a hyperglycemic hormone.

True Statement: Insulin acts mainly on hepatocytes and adipocytes, and enhances cellular glucose uptake and utilisation, resulting in decreased blood glucose levels (hypoglycemia).
False 1: Glucagon acts mainly on hepatocytes and adipocytes, and enhances cellular glucose uptake and utilisation, resulting in decreased blood glucose levels.
False 2: Insulin acts mainly on hepatocytes and adipocytes, and reduces cellular glucose uptake and utilisation, resulting in increased blood glucose levels.

True Statement: Insulin also stimulates conversion of glucose to glycogen (glycogenesis) in the target cells.
False 1: Glucagon also stimulates conversion of glucose to glycogen (glycogenesis) in the target cells.
False 2: Insulin also stimulates conversion of glycogen to glucose (glycogenolysis) in the target cells.

True Statement: Prolonged hyperglycemia leads to diabetes mellitus, associated with loss of glucose through urine and formation of harmful ketone bodies.
False 1: Prolonged hypoglycemia leads to diabetes mellitus.
False 2: Prolonged hyperglycemia leads to diabetes insipidus, associated with loss of glucose through urine.

True Statement: The Leydig cells (interstitial cells) present in the intertubular spaces of the testis produce androgens, mainly testosterone.
False 1: The Sertoli cells present in the seminiferous tubules of the testis produce androgens, mainly testosterone.
False 2: The Leydig cells of the testis produce estrogen and progesterone.

True Statement: Androgens regulate the development, maturation and functions of male accessory sex organs like epididymis, vas deferens, seminal vesicles, prostate gland and urethra.
False 1: Estrogens regulate the development, maturation and functions of male accessory sex organs like epididymis, vas deferens, seminal vesicles, prostate gland and urethra.

True Statement: Androgens stimulate muscular growth, growth of facial and axillary hair, aggressiveness, and low pitch of voice.
False 1: Estrogens stimulate muscular growth, growth of facial and axillary hair, aggressiveness, and low pitch of voice.
False 2: Androgens stimulate muscular growth, growth of facial and axillary hair, aggressiveness, and high pitch of voice.

True Statement: Androgens act on the central neural system and influence male sexual behaviour (libido).
False 1: Estrogens act on the central neural system and influence male sexual behaviour (libido).

True Statement: Androgens produce anabolic (synthetic) effects on protein and carbohydrate metabolism.
False 1: Estrogens produce anabolic (synthetic) effects on protein and carbohydrate metabolism.

True Statement: Estrogen is synthesised and secreted mainly by the growing ovarian follicles; after ovulation, the ruptured follicle is converted to corpus luteum, which secretes mainly progesterone.
False 1: Progesterone is synthesised and secreted mainly by the growing ovarian follicles; after ovulation, the corpus luteum secretes mainly estrogen.
False 2: Estrogen is synthesised and secreted mainly by the corpus luteum; progesterone is secreted by the growing ovarian follicles.

True Statement: Estrogens stimulate growth and activities of female secondary sex organs, development of ovarian follicles, and appearance of female secondary sex characters (e.g., high pitch of voice) and mammary gland development.
False 1: Progesterone stimulates growth and activities of female secondary sex organs and appearance of female secondary sex characters.
False 2: Estrogens stimulate appearance of male secondary sex characters, including low pitch of voice and growth of facial hair.

True Statement: Progesterone supports pregnancy and acts on mammary glands to stimulate formation of alveoli (sac-like structures which store milk) and milk secretion.
False 1: Estrogen supports pregnancy and acts on mammary glands to stimulate formation of alveoli and milk secretion.
False 2: Prolactin supports pregnancy and acts on mammary glands to stimulate formation of alveoli and milk secretion.

True Statement: The atrial wall of the heart secretes a peptide hormone called atrial natriuretic factor (ANF) which decreases blood pressure by causing dilation of blood vessels.
False 1: The ventricular wall of the heart secretes ANF which decreases blood pressure by causing dilation of blood vessels.
False 2: ANF increases blood pressure by causing constriction of blood vessels.

True Statement: The juxtaglomerular cells of the kidney produce a peptide hormone called erythropoietin which stimulates erythropoiesis (formation of RBC).
False 1: The juxtaglomerular cells of the kidney produce erythropoietin which stimulates leukopoiesis (formation of WBC).
False 2: The Bowman's capsule cells of the kidney produce erythropoietin which stimulates erythropoiesis.

True Statement: Gastrin acts on the gastric glands and stimulates the secretion of hydrochloric acid and pepsinogen.
False 1: Secretin acts on the gastric glands and stimulates the secretion of hydrochloric acid and pepsinogen.
False 2: Gastrin acts on the exocrine pancreas and stimulates the secretion of hydrochloric acid and pepsinogen.

True Statement: Secretin acts on the exocrine pancreas and stimulates secretion of water and bicarbonate ions.
False 1: Gastrin acts on the exocrine pancreas and stimulates secretion of water and bicarbonate ions.
False 2: Secretin acts on the gall bladder and stimulates secretion of water and bicarbonate ions.

True Statement: CCK (cholecystokinin) acts on both pancreas and gall bladder and stimulates secretion of pancreatic enzymes and bile juice respectively.
False 1: Secretin acts on both pancreas and gall bladder and stimulates secretion of pancreatic enzymes and bile juice respectively.
False 2: GIP acts on both pancreas and gall bladder and stimulates secretion of pancreatic enzymes and bile juice.

True Statement: GIP (gastric inhibitory peptide) inhibits gastric secretion and motility.
False 1: Gastrin inhibits gastric secretion and motility.
False 2: GIP stimulates gastric secretion and motility.

True Statement: Hormone receptors present on the cell membrane are called membrane-bound receptors; receptors present inside the target cell are called intracellular receptors (mostly nuclear receptors in the nucleus).
False 1: Hormone receptors present on the cell membrane are called intracellular receptors; those inside the target cell are called membrane-bound receptors.

True Statement: Hormones which interact with membrane-bound receptors normally do not enter the target cell, but generate second messengers (e.g., cyclic AMP, IP₃, Ca²⁺) which regulate cellular metabolism.
False 1: Hormones which interact with membrane-bound receptors normally enter the target cell and directly regulate gene expression.
False 2: Steroid hormones interact with membrane-bound receptors and generate second messengers such as cyclic AMP.

True Statement: Steroid hormones and iodothyronines interact with intracellular receptors and regulate gene expression or chromosome function.
False 1: Peptide and protein hormones interact with intracellular receptors and regulate gene expression or chromosome function.
False 2: Steroid hormones and iodothyronines interact with membrane-bound receptors and regulate gene expression.
